answer: Grading panels are drawn per submission, never per author, and the draw skips anyone within three hops of the author in the attestation graph. A ring that bought its own reviewers finds those keys filtered out. Voting from outside needs a grader with independent standing, six graded epochs deep, and the panel is redrawn every round, so bribery must cover every eligible reviewer rather than one. Fresh keys must climb the same vine before their judgment counts. Honest work takes the longer voyage and reaches the summit carrying a record purchased votes cannot imitate.
